input.question: Why is orange juice much cheaper than oranges?
input.ground_truth: Aside from the fact that juice manufacturers can buy in maybe bulk, thereby getting discounts, and aside from the fact that through futures (contracts that guarantee specified supply of oranges at a set price, irrespective of supply and demand spikes), oranges that you buy at the site are not the same as oranges for juicing. Store oranges are bred with size, color and hardiness in mind, whereas juicing oranges are bred for moisture content alone. Those moisture content oranges are cheaper to produce, and are produced at much greater quantities, altogether, this keeps the price low.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big basket of oranges. To make orange juice, you have to squeeze all those oranges and throw away the peels and seeds.

Now, when you buy a glass of orange juice, you are only getting the *juicy* part inside, not the whole orange with skin and all. The rest of the orange goes away.

But when you buy oranges, you get the whole orange – skin, seeds, and all! So, making juice from oranges means some of the orange is wasted.

Because of that, orange juice can be made cheaper from lots of oranges, and shops can sell it for less money than a whole orange. Also, big factories make juice very fast, so it’s even cheaper!

That’s why orange juice is often cheaper than buying oranges!
